competitor_patterns: Freshness signals dominate: Bikerumor and Cyclist explicitly timestamp updates (e.g. 'updated September 8, 2026') and add new products to existing guides, signalling continuous editorial maintenance rather than one-off posts.

Extreme word count depth: Tifosi's blog post hits 25,678 words and Cyclist's guide reaches 6,642 — both far exceeding a simple review format. Top-ranking content functions as exhaustive reference hubs, not standard buying guides.

Trusted third-party review integration: Bikerumor and Cyclist lead with 'Tested' or 'Reviewed' in their titles and structure content around hands-on editor testing methodology, lending credibility signals Google rewards with E-E-A-T.

FAQ + structured data ubiquity: Cyclist.co.uk includes both FAQs and dedicated 'How do I choose' H2 sections, making content eligible for FAQ rich snippets and People Also Ask boxes that inflate SERP real estate.

Categorical breadth within one URL: Top pages cover road, gravel, MTB, budget, and premium tiers all under a single high-authority URL rather than fragmenting into separate posts, consolidating topical authority and backlink equity.
our_gaps: No explicit 'last updated' timestamp or editorial update cadence: our posts lack visible freshness signals that Google's freshness algorithm rewards, especially for competitive 'best of 2026' queries where Bikerumor updated as recently as September 8.

Content fragmentation dilutes authority: we have 40+ separate posts covering adjacent subtopics instead of consolidating them into 2-3 authoritative hub pages (e.g. one master 'Best Cycling Glasses 2026' page with internal anchor links to subtopics), which disperses PageRank rather than concentrating it.

No comparison tables on the majority of posts (28 out of 40 lack tables): Tifosi and Cyclist use structured spec comparison tables that improve dwell time, scannability, and are frequently pulled into AI Overviews — we're missing this on posts directly targeting high-intent queries.

Missing independent third-party credibility signals: our posts are written from the brand's perspective. Top competitors cite their own testers, lab data, or quote external reviewers. We have no 'as tested by' framing, no rider testimonial quotes within content, and no reference to independent certification results.
